source: UnitedHealthcare public pages for members (uhc.com member resources, health insurance articles and consumer news articles, the start pages of its member forms at memberforms.uhc.com, and the member PDFs those pages link to), opened without signing in

pdf_renderer.check: Before rendering any PDF the tool downloads both files, compares their SHA-256 with these pinned values and stops on a mismatch; the checked bytes are the ones loaded into the page (the worker from a blob URL). The pinned files equal build/pdf.min.js and build/pdf.worker.min.js of the npm release pdfjs-dist 3.11.174.
pdf_renderer.rechecked: The PDF captures 02, 07, 12 and 13, made on 2026-11-27 with pdf.js loaded from the same URLs before this check existed, were rendered again with the checked files on 2026-11-28 and matched the committed screenshots byte for byte.

note: Screenshots of public pages and documents, kept as review evidence only. The App copies no branding, text or images from them. Floating site elements (the cookie notice, the feedback tab and the survey invitation) are hidden before each web capture; the page content is unchanged. The web pages captured show no personal data. PDF pages are rendered with pdf.js and cropped to the region named in each entry. The publisher's sample statement carries placeholder member data (a test name and mailing address, member ID, group name and number, patient account and claim numbers); these are covered by grey boxes like personal data, the capture stops if any of them is found outside a box, and each entry lists what was covered and what was left visible. Width and height are read from the saved PNG. Most workflows have no public image of the member portal, which is behind sign-in; for those, articles, form start pages, the blank claim form and the sample statement stand in, each entry with text_alternative says what it stands in for, and the workflow is marked alternative proposed, reviewer agreement pending.

workflows.gap: The member portal screen for giving a family member or representative access is behind sign-in. The closest public reference is the start page of the plan's form for releasing health information and filing a power of attorney (01).

workflows.status: Screenshots of the publisher's sample statement
workflows.gap: The member portal's claim list is behind sign-in. A claim with its lines is shown on the publisher's sample explanation of benefits (02), and the article on reading an EOB lists what it contains (03).

workflows.status: Alternative proposed; 04 and 05 are public consumer articles from the reference product, not product pages; reviewer agreement pending
workflows.gap: No public page shows a plan's information request to a member or a revised EOB. The closest public text: why claims go to further review (04), the letters sent while a claim is reviewed (05) and what to do when an EOB looks wrong (06).

No public page shows the plan's questions on other coverage or an accident as a member answers them. The plan's public medical claim form asks both (07), and its coordination of benefits notice says members are asked to identify every plan that covers the family (08).

No public page shows a prior authorization's status in the portal or an expedite request. The closest public text: how prior authorization works and how long it takes (09), and that a provider can ask for a faster review (10).

No public page shows the portal's appeal screens, and no public page describes withdrawing an appeal. The closest public references: the start page of the plan's appeal request form (11), and the appeal rights printed on the sample statement: an appeal in writing within 180 days, by the member or an authorized representative such as a family member, with comments, documents or other information (12).

workflows.status: Screenshots of the publisher's sample statement
workflows.gap: The portal's plan balances screen is behind sign-in. The sample statement's plan balances show deductible and out-of-pocket progress (13), and the article explains individual and family limits (14).
